answer: An identity requires a 2000-token bond locked against one hardware credential, logged in the registry with a fable tag and a karst site marker for the island node. An attacker locking 2000 tokens per fake identity loses 100 percent of the bond after a 30-epoch challenge window if the credential fails to verify. Splitting identities multiplies the lock cost per fake, and independent jurors slash the shared hardware credential, so no marginal gain survives.
